The thumbs point inwards on the backs of the hands, outwards on the palms.

Left is blue, right is red, the centre is yellow and the root is purple. The Body page is a front view: the character's left is on your right. Hands & Feet View sets the other two pages (their drawings turn with them): Front (the default): the same front view as the Body page. The right hand and foot are on the left, fingers and toes point down, wrists and heels are at the top. Own: as you see your own hands and feet. Left is on the left, fingers and toes point up. Big toes point inwards in both views. Thumbs point inwards with the backs of the hands, outwards with the palms (Hands Side).
Each shape is bound to the bone of the same name. Bones your rig doesn't have are skipped, and a warning lists them. A page with none of its bones gets no tab.

Add the chart to a picker that already has one and you get a second chart, on pages of its own named Body.001, Hands.001 and so on, and a warning says so. Undo removes it. Note: Rigify's human metarig has one toe per foot, so the per-toe shapes are skipped unless you add toe bones named toe1.01.L to toe5.03.L with the limbs.super_finger rig type (see Toes for Rigify below). The demo files do this. Missing toes get their own short note, so a real naming problem elsewhere still shows.

To get one control per toe, do this on the metarig before you generate: Add five toe chains to each foot. Name them toe1.01.L (big toe) to toe5.03.L. The big toe has two bones, the others three. Give the first bone of each chain the limbs.super_finger rig type. Rigify then makes a tip, a master and an FK control per segment. Put them in their own bone collection, for example "Toes". The Rigify Male Body Picker and Rigify Female Body Picker demo files have toes made this way.

entries.h: Use the shapes in your own picker
entries.t: The shapes are stored in the picker, so they travel with the .blend (the drawings too: they are packed). Any Geometry Shape of the same picker can use them: Add a Geometry Shape widget. Open its Custom Shape panel. Pick a shape under Canvas shapes. Set its bone, colour and size as usual. You can also delete the shapes you don't need, or move them to make your own layout.

Two demos show the result: Rigify Male Body Picker and Rigify Female Body Picker. Each has a generated rig with toes and a Rigify face, the four pages over their drawings (the Face page over the male or the female face), the IK/FK puck beside each IK hand and foot, a Rig Settings frame with the head and neck follow knobs and the IK stretch sliders, and bone collection toggles. Open them from the demo list.
Make the picker for the generated rig (the RIG-... object you animate), not for the metarig. Select it and enter Pose Mode. Set an area to Armature Picker. Click New Picker.

In the 3D Viewport, select the controls you want buttons for: the torso, hips, chest and head controls, the hand and foot IK controls, the FK controls, the fingers... Click Import Selected Bones on the card (or Utils > Import Selected Bones in Edit Mode). Click to place each button. Left and right controls come in pairs. Tip: Repeat with more bones whenever you like. Bones that already have a button are skipped.

Rigify names its controls with .L and .R, so the picker pairs them. In Edit Mode, move, resize or rotate the left button and the right one follows, mirrored across the red centre line. Centre controls (torso, chest, head) stay on the line.

Rigify limbs switch between IK and FK with an IK_FK property (0 is IK, 1 is FK) on the limb's ..._parent control. A bone picker can show a small puck that flips it: In Edit Mode, select the button of a limb control, for example hand_ik.L or upper_arm_fk.L. In the sidebar Widget tab, find the IK/FK row and click the armature button at its end (Rigify IK/FK). FlexSpace reads the rig's drivers to find the right limb and sets everything: the Data Path (pose.bones["upper_arm_parent.L"]["IK_FK"]) and IK Value: Min. If it can't tell the limb, it lists every bone with an IK_FK property, the same side first. In Pose Mode, click the puck to switch. The puck: shows the current state, follows the property when you change it elsewhere, is keyed when Auto Keying is on, makes every click one undo step. Toggle Size sets its size. Tip: Not Rigify? Choose Bone (a custom property of a bone, with a list of its bool, int and float properties) or Data Path, and set IK Value to the end that means IK.

Rigify sorts its controls into bone collections (Torso, Arm.L (IK), Arm.L (FK), Fingers...). Add a toggle for each one you show and hide often: In Edit Mode, press Shift A > Bone Picker > Bone Collection. Pick the collection and place it. Choose Visible or Solo in its Bone Collection panel. With Sync Bone Collections Visibility on (sidebar, Armature tab), the buttons of hidden collections hide too, so the picker matches the viewport. The Face page of Humanoid Body (Rigify) (and the Face page of the Rigify Human Picker demo) is a good start for your own face picker. Every face control of Rigify's human sits on the drawn feature of a face picture, coloured by side (left blue, right red, centre yellow): Eyes: a ring around each eye moves the whole eye (master_eye), a dot on the pupil aims it (eye), almond segments on the lash lines move the lids, and the EYES bar on the forehead moves the common eye target. Brows: three arched strips on each brow, and a row of dots under it. Nose, cheeks, lips and jaw: the nose master is the diamond on the bridge, the lips are arcs above and below the mouth line with a dot at each corner, the JAW bar is under the chin. Teeth & Tongue: the open mouth in its own frame, the upper and lower teeth and the tongue with its chain. Expressions: a Gaze (Eyes) pad bound to the eye target, a pad per mouth corner, and knobs for Mouth Lock and Eyes Follow. The face picture is a locked Backdrop Image, so clicks go through it to the controls. The lighter controls are the finer ones of the Face (Secondary) collection, the darker ones are masters.

Rigify puts many settings on its controls as custom properties (IK stretch, follow, FK limb follow...). To bind a slider to one: Add Data > Numbers > Lineal. Click the eyedropper next to Data Path. Right-click the property in the 3D Viewport sidebar (Item tab, Rig Main Properties, or the bone's Custom Properties). The rig follows while you drag: the drivers that read the property update as it changes. Knobs, Number Fields and Enums bound to custom properties work the same way. Tip: For IK / FK, use the puck beside the IK hand or foot (see 4. The IK/FK puck) instead of a slider: one click switches the limb, and the puck shows which way it is.

Buttons remember their bone by name and by a hidden bone id, so they follow renamed bones. If you regenerate the rig, change bone names in the metarig, or paste buttons from another picker: Open the picker in Edit Mode and run Utils > Repair Bone Bindings. It follows renamed bones, binds buttons by bone name, and reports the bones still missing. Buttons with a Missing bone badge need a new bone: pick it in the Bone field. If the picker shows Not the picker of ... after regenerating, click Use it for ... on the card to give it back to the rig.

Every recipe uses the same few moves: Make a canvas and set its page's mode (the icon next to the page in the sidebar's Pages panel, see The Canvas > Pages and modes). One canvas can hold a page per mode: it shows the right one when you change mode. In Edit Mode, Shift A adds a widget. Shift A > From Property adds one already bound to a property you right-click. From anywhere, right-click a property or button > Add to FlexSpace Canvas does the same without opening the canvas. Ctrl J puts the selected widgets in a Frame. Give it a Title and a colour. Tab goes back to Live Mode to use the canvas. Tip: Want to see the finished version first? Open the matching demo (Help > Demo Files) and take it apart.

entries.h: FlexSpace Studio: one canvas for every mode
entries.t: The FlexSpace Studio demo is one canvas with a Home page and a page for each mode, and one scene with an object for each page: a Geometry Nodes tower, a shader ball, a head to sculpt, a box to paint, a rigged arm and a Grease Pencil drawing. Change the mode and the canvas changes with it. The recipes below build its pages one by one. You will need: a Flex Space canvas with one page per mode, and an object that can enter each mode. Make the canvas. Add a page per mode with the + next to the page selector, and set each page's mode in the Pages panel of the sidebar (N): for example Object Mode, Sculpt Mode, Texture Paint, Weight Paint and Draw Mode. Keep Switch Pages Automatically on (the Pages panel). Now Ctrl Tab, or the mode menu in the 3D Viewport header, also changes the canvas to that mode's page. Two pages can share a mode: the first one shows, and you pick the other from its tab. A page made for an object (Show When > Object) shows when you select that object. Build each page in Edit Mode (Tab). Edit Mode works in any Blender mode, so you don't have to enter the mode first. Add a note on each page: a Frame whose Title says which mode it is for, coloured like the mode, with a Label or two in it. Add Try it buttons to the note: Operator buttons that run Enter Mode (flexspace.enter_mode). Set its Mode, its Object and View Object. A click makes that object active and selected, frames it in the 3D Viewport and enters the mode, and the canvas shows the mode's page. Add a default page as the first tab: a Home page with Show When > Always. Switch Pages Automatically shows the most specific page that fits, and Always is the least specific, so Home only shows when no other page does. Without it, leaving Sculpt Mode with the head still active would leave the canvas on the Sculpt page, dimmed because it no longer fits. Give Home a welcome note and a button for each of the other pages. Tip: Enter Mode takes no text, only choices, so its buttons run at once, even in a file that can't run scripts. Demo file: FlexSpace Studio. It opens in Object Mode on the Object page. Home has a button for each page, and every other page has the note and a Try it button for each of the other modes.

You will need: an object with a Geometry Nodes modifier, an Object Mode page, Enums, Number Fields, Sliders, Toggles, a Color Picker, a Color Palette, a Script button, a List and Frames. Select the object, and set the page's Show When to Object in Mode: Object Mode, with the tower as its Object (Use Active). The page now shows while the tower is active in Object Mode. Bind widgets to the modifier's inputs by their path, for example active_object.modifiers["GeometryNodes"].properties.inputs.Socket_2.value. To get an input's path, right-click it in the modifier panel and choose Copy Data Path, then put active_object. in front. Pin each widget to the object, so the canvas keeps driving it when another object is active. A Menu Switch input is an enum: an Enum set to Segmented shows its items as buttons. Use Number Fields for counts (Floors, Windows), Sliders for sizes (Width, Taper, Twist) and Toggles for on/off inputs (Balconies, Trees). Add a Color Picker bound to a colour input. To use it in a material, store the colour with a Store Named Attribute node and read it with an Attribute node in the material. A Color Palette with a few ready colours goes under it. For a Randomize button, add a Script button that sets the Seed input to random.randint(0, 9999). Add a List with its Source set to Material Slots: click a row to select the material, then a slider for its roughness (active_object.active_material...). Frame the blocks: Shape, Details, Scatter, Materials and Colour. Note: A Script button runs code saved in the file. In a file you don't trust, Flex Space asks once before it runs it. In the demo: the tower on its plaza with trees, made by one Geometry Nodes modifier.

You will need: a page made for the shader ball, Color Pickers, Sliders, Number Fields, Toggles and Frames. Add a page, select the shader ball, and set the page's Show When to Object, with Use Active. Now selecting the ball shows this page. Add a Color Picker for the material's Base Color, and sliders for Roughness and Metallic. Pin them to the object. Add a Color Picker for the world colour and a Number Field for its Strength. Add a Color Picker and a Number Field for the key light's colour and Power, and a swatch and a field for the rim light. Pin each one to its light. Add toggles for the 3D Viewport's Scene World and Scene Lights. Material Preview ignores the scene's lights and world without them. In the demo: the shader ball, the studio's key and rim lights, and the world.

You will need: a Sculpt Mode page, Brush Pickers, Sliders, an Enum, Toggles, Operator buttons and Frames. Add a page and set its mode to Sculpt Mode. Add the brushes: Shift A > Buttons > Brush Picker. In the sidebar, Choose Brush picks one, for example Draw, Clay Strips, Inflate, Smooth, Flatten or Grab. Add one per brush. Group them by job. Select a few and press Ctrl J to frame them: for example Basic, Smooth & Flatten, Detail and Masking. Add the stroke: sliders for Radius and Strength, an Enum for the brush Direction, and X, Y, Z toggles for symmetry. From Property on the tool settings is the quickest way. Add Operator buttons for Voxel Remesh, Symmetrize, the mask tools and the face set tools. Add the viewport rows: Set Value toggles for Solid and Material shading and for Matcap and Studio lighting, toggles for Wireframe and X-Ray, and a Dyntopo button. Tip: Turn on the unified radius and strength in Blender's tool settings. Then one slider works for every brush. In the demo: a base head ready to sculpt.

You will need: a Texture Paint page, a Color Picker, a Color Palette, Brush Pickers, Sliders, Toggles, Operator buttons and Frames. Add a page and set its mode to Texture Paint. Its object needs UVs and an image in its material. Add a Color Picker bound to the paint colour. Set its Shape to Ring + Square and turn on RGB and HSV under Show. Add a Swap button next to it for the secondary colour. Add a Color Palette under it, bound to the same colour. Set its Source to Palette to use a Blender palette. Add Brush Pickers for the paint brushes, in framed blocks: for example Paint (Paint Hard, Paint Soft, Airbrush), Blend & Fill (Smear, Blur, Clone, Fill) and Erase & Mask. Add brush settings (radius and strength sliders), toggles for the mask, the stencil and symmetry, and viewport toggles. Finish with a Save All Images button, so your painting is never lost. Tip: Turn on the unified colour in Blender's tool settings. Then every brush paints with the colour of the picker. In the demo: a rounded box with a few dabs of paint on its image.

You will need: a Weight Paint page, Brush Pickers, Sliders, Enums, Toggles, Operator buttons and Frames. Add a page and set its mode to Weight Paint. Its object is a rigged mesh. Add Brush Pickers for the weight brushes in two framed blocks: Paint (Set Weight, Add Weight) and Blend (Blur, Average, Smear). Add the brush: sliders for radius and strength, Enums for the blend and the falloff. Add a Brush Weight slider. Under it, a row of small Operator buttons for quick values: 0, .25, .5, .75 and 1. Add toggles for Auto Normalize, Multi-Paint, Lock-Relative and Restrict, and for mirror symmetry. Add Operator buttons to clean up the vertex groups, and viewport toggles for zero weights, contours and wireframe. Note: A Set Value toggle only takes enums and integers. For the quick weight buttons, use Operator buttons that set the value instead. In the demo: a rigged arm. Enter Mode selects its armature too, so Ctrl click a bone to paint its group.

You will need: a Draw Mode page, Brush Pickers, a Color Picker, a Color Palette, a List, Sliders, Toggles, Operator buttons and Frames. Add a page and set its mode to Draw Mode. Its object is a Grease Pencil object. Add a Color Picker and a Color Palette for the brush colour. Set the Color Mode to Vertex Color, so that colour is the one drawn. Add Brush Pickers for the draw brushes in framed blocks: Pencils & Inks, Markers & Fill, and Erasers. Add buttons for the material slots, and a Stroke block: radius, strength, pressure and the stabilizer. Add a Layers block: a List with its Source set to Grease Pencil Layers (click a layer to make it active, the eye and lock on each row, + and − to add and remove), and a slider for the active layer's opacity. Then add an Animation block: Prev Key, Play, Next Key, Insert Blank Keyframe and onion skinning. Add a Canvas block with toggles for the grid and the guides. In the demo: a small drawing on three layers (Sketch, Color, Ink) and a ball keyed on three frames.

You will need: a rig generated with Rigify, an Armature Picker, and the Humanoid Body (Rigify) chart. Select the generated rig (not the metarig) and enter Pose Mode. Set an area to Armature Picker and click New Picker. Press Tab for Edit Mode, then Shift A > Bone Picker > Humanoid Body (Rigify). Pick the Body (Adult Male or Adult Female), the pages (Body, Hands, Feet), the Scale, and turn on IK/FK Switches. Keep Character Backdrop on to have the drawing behind each page. Press Tab and click a shape to pick its bone. Tip: Rigify's human metarig has one toe per foot. For a control per toe, add toe chains before you generate (see Picker with Rigify). Demo files: Rigify Male Body Picker and Rigify Female Body Picker.
Demo files are small, finished scenes that show what you can build. Open one to try it, take it apart, or copy what you like into your own work.

There are three ways in: The Open a Demo link on the card in the middle of an empty editor. Help > Demo Files in the header of the editor. Preferences > Add-ons > FlexSpace: the Demo Files section lists every demo with its picture. In the editor, the demo browser opens over it: The categories on the left group the demos: armature pickers, control panels, modes and pages, brushes, Geometry Nodes. Type to search: the cards show the demos whose title or description has the words. Click a card to choose it, then Open in New Window. A double-click, or Enter, opens it right away. Esc, a right click or a click outside the browser closes it. From the preferences, a dialog shows the demo with its Open in New Window button.

entries.h: A copy in its own window
entries.t: A demo always opens in another Blender window, as a copy of the demo file in a temporary folder. Your open file and its window are not touched. Keep working in it while the demo is open. The copy is temporary. Use File > Save As to keep it anywhere you like. The demo file that comes with FlexSpace never changes. Open it again as new, as many times as you like.

FlexSpace Studio shows how one canvas follows Blender's mode. It has a Home page and a page for each mode (Object, Look Dev, Sculpt, Texture Paint, Weight Paint and Draw), and a scene with an object for each one. It opens in Object Mode on the Object page. Home shows when no other page fits, for example in Object Mode with the head selected. Its buttons take you to every other page. Change the mode with Ctrl Tab or the mode menu in the 3D Viewport header, and the canvas shows that mode's page. Or click a Try it button in the note at the top of a page: it selects the right object, frames it and enters the mode. The recipes build it page by page (see Recipes).

Sculpt Wheel is a Ring Menu for Sculpt Mode. It opens in Sculpt Mode on a base head. The outer ring has every Essentials sculpt brush. The everyday ones are on the first page; click the tab under the ring for the others. The inner ring has X symmetry, automasking, Dyntopo, Voxel Remesh and mask operators. Next to it are a round Favorites frame of round brush buttons, and square brush buttons with the radius and strength.

City Builder is a procedural island city made by six Geometry Nodes systems: the island, the sea, the streets with their traffic, the buildings, the forest and the street lights. One canvas page drives all of them. It opens in Live Mode next to the 3D Viewport in Material Preview with the scene's lights and world (EEVEE, the same picture as Rendered), at golden hour. Buildings: drag Grow to raise the city from its empty plots, then try Floors, Density, Style, Rooftops (zoom in on the roofs to see it) and Seed. Night: drag Nightfall. The sun sets, the sky turns to sunset and blue hour, the windows and the street lamps light up, and the night falls. Window Light picks the colour of the lit windows. Island, Roads and Forest reshape the land, the street grid and the trees. The widgets are bound to the inputs of the Geometry Nodes modifiers (Window Light to the buildings' material): rest the mouse on one to read what it does. The modifier panel of each object in the Properties editor (the Geometry Nodes workspace has one) shows the same values. The file has no Python scripts: it works with Auto Run Python Scripts off. Tip: EEVEE needs a capable graphics card. If the 3D Viewport feels slow, switch it to Solid in its header: the canvas works the same.

Some demos drive lights, the world or materials. Their 3D Viewport opens in Material Preview with Scene Lights and Scene World on, so you see the changes. Note: Material Preview ignores the scene's lights unless those are on (the viewport's Shading popover). Rendered shading always shows them.

A small product-shot scene (three lights, Suzanne, a cube and a sphere, a turntable animation) with a control panel for it: light power, colour, size and shadows, the scene's render and playback settings, modifiers, material colours and a camera preview.

A control panel for the viewport and the scene: shading buttons and X-Ray for the 3D Viewport, object display settings, the world colour, the camera's lens and depth of field, the frame range and the render engine and resolution. It comes with a small scene to try it on.

Animation controls on a canvas: playback buttons, the current frame, the frame and preview ranges, the frame rate, Auto Keying and the keyframe type, Insert and Delete Keyframe. It comes with a bouncing ball to try them on.

One canvas that follows Blender's mode and the active object: a page for each mode, and the scene for all of them, with a Home page when nothing else fits. The tower in Object Mode shows its Geometry Nodes controls, the shader ball a Look Dev page for its material, world and lights, Sculpt Mode a base head, Texture Paint a box, Weight Paint a rigged arm and Draw Mode a Grease Pencil drawing. Switch the mode, select an object, or click a Try it button, and the canvas shows that page.

A Ring Menu for Sculpt Mode: every Essentials sculpt brush in its outer ring (the tab under it flips pages), symmetry, automasking, Dyntopo, Voxel Remesh and mask operators in its inner ring, the hovered item's name in the middle. Around it, a round Favorites frame of round brush buttons and a block of square ones with the radius and strength. It opens in Sculpt Mode on a base head.

A procedural island city made by six Geometry Nodes systems (the island, the sea, the streets with their traffic, the buildings, the forest and the street lights), all driven from one canvas. Grow the city from its empty plots, stretch the skyline, change the style and the seed, reshape the island and the street grid, plant the forest, then drag Nightfall: the sun sets, the windows and the street lamps light up and the sky goes to night. It opens in Material Preview with the scene's lights and world: the full EEVEE look.

Find what you see, then read its cause and its fix.

Symptom Cause Fix The picker shows a card instead of your buttons The picker only works on its own armature, in Pose Mode. The card says what is missing, and its button fixes it: Enter Pose Mode, Pose "rig" (makes that rig active) or Use it for ... (gives this picker to the active armature). See The Armature Picker. Some picker buttons say "Missing bone" Their bone was deleted or renamed in a way FlexSpace couldn't follow (for example after regenerating a rig). In Edit Mode, run Utils > Repair Bone Bindings, then pick a new bone for the ones still missing. Some picker buttons are gone Sync Bone Collections Visibility (sidebar, Armature tab) hides the buttons of bones in hidden collections. Show the collection, or turn the option off. Some widgets are gone The View Object Types menu at the end of the header hides whole widget types. Turn the type back on there. Some widgets are gone They are on another page. Check the page selector in the header. A widget has a dashed outline in Edit Mode Its binding doesn't work: the path is wrong, or it points to the wrong kind of property. Select it and read the note under its Data Path in the sidebar. See Binding Properties. The top bar says ⚠ N broken or N unbound That many widgets have a broken binding or none yet, on the pages that work in the current mode and with the active object. Click it: it selects and frames the next broken widget (on its page) and opens the sidebar's Widget tab. Fix its path there, then click again for the next one. The count is gone once all are fixed. An operator button is red Its operator can't run right now, for example a Pose Mode tool with no armature in Pose Mode. Use it in the right mode, or pick another operator. A button asks "Run Untrusted Code?" The button runs code stored in the .blend file, and Blender's Auto Run Python Scripts is off (or the file is in an excluded folder). Click Trust and Run if you trust the file. FlexSpace asks once per session, and again if the script changes. Shift A does nothing Widgets are added in Edit Mode. Press Tab first. A key does something unexpected Canvas keys come first (see Shortcuts). Any other key goes on to Blender's own keymap, so your custom bindings apply. Check the key in Shortcuts, or in your own Blender keymap. The widgets look wrong, too dark or too light The theme Appearance doesn't suit your editor, or a widget has Override Theme on and keeps its own colours. Check Appearance in View > Theme (Auto follows the Node Editor background). For a widget with its own colours, click Reset to Theme in its Style panel. Note: In the picker, the rig must also be in Pose Mode before Shift A adds widgets, and your Pose Mode keys work as in the 3D Viewport.

Found something broken? Open Help > Report a Bug... in the canvas header (or Report a Bug in the add-on preferences). Write a title, what happened, the steps to make it happen again, and what you expected. FlexSpace adds the details for you: the Blender and FlexSpace versions, your system and GPU, the canvas, the modules and the last FlexSpace errors of this session. Click Open on GitHub: a new issue opens in your browser, filled in. Review it and submit it there. No GitHub account? Click Copy Report and paste it in a comment on the product page or in an email. Nothing is sent by FlexSpace itself, and your home folder in any file path is replaced by ~.
